# Section 9: Educational Program Structure and Content

Section 9 addresses program structure, general education, and academic content requirements.

## Standard 9.1 — Program Content [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Educational programs are of appropriate quality and academic content.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Course catalog and program requirements
- Course syllabi
- Curriculum review processes
- External validation (advisory committees, accreditation)

### Suggested Owners

- Chief Academic Officer
- Curriculum Committee
- Program Directors

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Programs lack rigor documentation
- No systematic curriculum review process
- Outdated course content

---

## Standard 9.2 — Program Length [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Program length is appropriate for its degree level and comparable to similar programs at other institutions.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Credit hour requirements by program
- Comparison with similar programs
- Rationale for any unusual requirements

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Programs significantly shorter or longer than peers without justification

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community college programs follow SBCC curriculum standards:

- **AAS/AS/AA degrees:** Typically 60-76 semester hours
- **Diplomas:** Typically 36-48 semester hours
- **Certificates:** Typically 12-18 semester hours

Reference SBCC Curriculum Standards and Combined Course Library requirements.
:::

---

## Standard 9.3 — General Education Requirements [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Degree programs have a substantial general education component with breadth across major areas.

### Typical Evidence Types

- General education requirements by degree
- Mapping of courses to areas of knowledge
- Credit hour analysis

### Requirements by Degree Level

- **Associate:** At least 15 semester hours
- **Baccalaureate (if applicable):** At least 30 semester hours

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges follow the Universal General Education Transfer Component (UGETC) aligned with the Comprehensive Articulation Agreement (CAA). Document:

- General education course requirements
- CAA alignment
- UGETC course designations
:::

---

## Standard 9.4 — Institutional Credit for Degree

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

A minimum of 25% of credit hours for each degree must be earned through instruction offered by the institution.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Transfer credit policies
- Analysis of institutional credit requirements
- Graduation audit procedures

---

## Standard 9.5 — Academic Policies

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Academic policies are established and published.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Catalog academic policies
- Add/drop policies
- Grading policies
- Academic integrity policies

---

## Standard 9.6 — Post-Secondary Credit

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution awards credit based on documented student achievement of learning outcomes.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Credit hour policies
- Course contact hour documentation
- Policies on credit for prior learning

---

## Standard 9.7 — Program Curriculum

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Programs follow coherent curricula with stated purposes, content, and learning outcomes.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Program descriptions with outcomes
- Curriculum maps
- Course sequence documentation
- Prerequisites documentation

---

## Reflective Prompts

- How do we ensure program content remains current and rigorous?
- What processes verify general education breadth across programs?
- How is credit hour policy consistently applied?
